sections.html:
Des Moines is a King County city on the east shore of Puget Sound with 33,032 residents (July 1, 2025). Federal Way lies to the south, Kent to the east, SeaTac to the northeast, Burien to the north and Normandy Park to the northwest. That puts a house within reach of Sea-Tac Airport, the I-5 corridor and the water. Sea-Tac sits about 2 miles to the north, and some property in the city has been bought out because of aircraft noise, a topic buyers raise.

With 39.4 percent of households renting, many sales involve a tenant. The mean commute of 30.8 minutes is why buyers weigh the new light rail station and highway access so closely.

Most of the city rolls down to Puget Sound from about 400 feet along Pacific Highway, which gives many homes a view of the water and Vashon Island. The ravines of Des Moines Creek and Massey Creek cut through that slope. If your lot is near either ravine, expect buyers to ask about drainage, flooding and slope stability, topics the state seller disclosure form raises directly.

  • Marina and downtown: an 838-berth city marina with a fishing pier and boat launch.
  • Zenith and Woodmont: Saltwater State Park sits in a steep ravine between them.
  • Redondo: a boardwalk and aquarium near the Federal Way border.
  • Kent-Des Moines Road area: a park-and-ride with express buses, plus Highline College and a Central Washington University branch.

Highline Public Schools covers most of Des Moines, with Pacific Middle School and Mount Rainier High School as the local secondary schools. Woodmont and Redondo are in the Federal Way School District, so a few streets share a city but not a district.

Interstate 5 and State Routes 99, 509 and 516 serve the city. The Kent Des Moines light rail station on the 1 Line opened in December 2025 near Highline College. King County Metro buses run to the Burien Transit Center and Kent station, and the park-and-ride at the Kent-Des Moines Road interchange has express service to Seattle and Tacoma. Mention the station and the park-and-ride in a listing for any house within reach of them.

An owner who rents a home for stays of 30 nights or less needs both a city business license and a short-term rental permit, along with a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. The city's rules include:

  • A local property representative must be reachable around the clock and respond to complaints within 30 minutes.
  • Only one booking at a time is allowed per dwelling unit, and occupancy follows a city table.
  • No overnight street parking, and the owner must contract for garbage service.
  • Violations can lead to permit denial or revocation and infractions.

Business licenses are filed and renewed each year through FileLocal. A business outside the city needs one only if it earns $4,000 or more a year in Des Moines. If you hold a permit, ask the Community Development office whether it transfers to a buyer, since the answer depends on the permit terms. The office counter is open Tuesday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., at 21630 11th Avenue S, Suite D.

Sellers here usually weigh four approaches against their deadline and the home's condition:

  • List on the market: best for updated homes with water views or close access to the light rail.
  • Sell as-is to an investor: fits deferred repairs, tenant-occupied homes and inherited houses.
  • Sell to a cash buyer: removes loan approval delays, and the closing date can usually be set to your schedule.
  • Sell by owner: saves the agent fee, but you manage disclosure forms and the closing paperwork.

If a tenant lives in the house, check the lease, the notice rules and whether the buyer wants vacant possession before you accept an offer. Compare bids by net proceeds, after excise tax, any loan payoff and prorated taxes.

Washington's state excise tax rises with price under RCW 82.45.060. It takes 1.1 percent of the portion up to $525,000 and 1.28 percent of the portion from $525,000 up to $1,525,000. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the first tier moves to $551,000. Sellers usually bear it. Payment is made to the treasurer of the county holding the property, and a local rate is layered on.

Before closing, ask King County for the current excise tax affidavit steps and the combined local rate for Des Moines, and have your escrow officer show the tax line on the settlement statement.

Under RCW 84.56.020 the full bill is due April 30. Owners whose total reaches $50 may instead pay half in April and half by October 31. If you are selling, check the parcel for unpaid second-half tax. Statements are due to be distributed by March 15 when the county has the tax roll on time.

A late home of four or fewer units owes 9 percent interest per year but no penalties. Other property faces 12 percent plus penalties of 3 percent and then 8 percent. Get the exact payoff from King County Treasury Operations before closing, since escrow uses that figure to settle the account.

sections.h2: What to prepare before you list
sections.html:
Gather the lease and notice records if a tenant lives there, permit history for any work, a short-term rental permit if you hold one, and your latest tax statement. If your lot is near a ravine, be ready to answer drainage and slope questions on the disclosure form. A clean file makes both a regular buyer and a cash buyer more comfortable.

After you accept an offer, escrow opens and title work turns up any unpaid property tax. You sign the deed and affidavit, and escrow pays the excise tax shown on the settlement statement from what you receive. Cash means no loan approval, so the closing date tends to follow title work and the tenant's situation, if you have one. Ask your closing agent what the combined local rate will be so the net figure holds no surprises.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Des Moines?
faqs.a: Highline Public Schools covers most of Des Moines. Woodmont and Redondo belong to the Federal Way School District, so confirm your own address.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Des Moines?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes, a city business license and a short-term rental permit, backed by a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. Complaints must get an answer from a local representative within 30 minutes.

faqs.q: How is the state excise tax figured on a Des Moines sale?
faqs.a: By tier. The first $525,000 pays 1.1 percent, and the next slice to $1,525,000 pays 1.28 percent. Add the local rate. The seller normally covers it.

faqs.q: Is Sea-Tac Airport near Des Moines?
faqs.a: Yes. The airport is about 2 miles north of the city, and some Des Moines property has been bought out because of aircraft noise. Ask the county or an agent about noise context for a specific address.

faqs.q: When are King County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 is the due date, though a total of $50 or more can be split with the second half due October 31. Look for unpaid second-half tax before you sell.
